response.consequence: If getCalendar or the calendar's deleteEvent fails during a reschedule, the error is not logged by the intended handler. It surfaces as an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process on newer Node versions or in serverless runtimes. Calendar deletions may also be cut off when the request ends.
response.explanation: In vital/lib/reschedule.ts and wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, the forEach callback was changed to async so that `await getCalendar(...)` could be used. forEach does not await the callback's promise, so the surrounding try/catch (which logs errors) can no longer catch a rejection from getCalendar, from the dynamic import of the app, or from deleteEvent. These rejections become unhandled promise rejections. The deletions are also not awaited, so the function continues before they finish. The same pattern was added in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx (requestReschedule, around line 553), which has no try/catch at all.
response.title: try/catch no longer covers calendar lookup after forEach callback became async
